audit_result.proof_trace: The property requires both Merkle roots to be immutable after publishSaleResults(), but setAcceptedCapital() lacks the whenSaleResultsNotPublished guard that is applied to other post-publish-sensitive functions (cancel, transferInvestorPosition). It carries only onlyLegion + whenSaleNotCanceled guards, allowing overwrite of acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot at any time post-publication. claimTokensMerkleRoot is immutable (no setter), but acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot is not — proof fails at LegionAbstractSale.sol:438.
audit_result.attack_scenario: The Legion admin calls publishSaleResults() to finalize accepted capital, then calls setAcceptedCapital(maliciousRoot) to replace acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot; investors whose proofs were valid against the original root can no longer call withdrawExcessInvestedCapital (L767 reverts), while investors with proofs against the new root gain access — enabling arbitrary post-hoc redistribution of accepted capital.

PROP-01b-partial-inv-011.text: Merkle roots (claimMerkleRoot, acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot) are immutable after publishSaleResults.
PROP-01b-partial-inv-011.assertion: publishSaleResults() sets roots AND no subsequent function modifies claimMerkleRoot or acceptedCapitalMerkleRoot
